cardTexts.card-fundamentals: 🏢 Fundamentals ◇ INFO Is the business behind the stock in trouble? Facts, not a score. Not applicable This is an ETF. It holds many companies, so there's no single business to check. Next earnings · No earnings date found in the feed. How these checks were chosen Sales falling 10% or more: fast-shrinking sales are a real risk over a multi-week hold, even with a clean chart (traders who buy growth, like O'Neil, look for growing businesses). Depending on the source, the number is the latest quarter vs a year ago or the last fiscal year. Negative return on equity: the feed's return on equity is below zero, which usually means net income was negative. A plain fact. Companies with negative equity (some heavy buyback names) can show a negative ROE even when profitable. Debt/Equity above 2.0: heavy borrowing. Banks, utilities and REITs carry high debt by design, so a flag on those is weaker. Next earnings: O'Neil and Minervini avoid holding a fresh swing trade through a report, because the price can gap far past any stop. Highlighted within the app's 7-day earnings warning window. Left out on purpose: earnings growth (O'Neil's "C"): STA's field is a year-over-year rate that swings wildly when last year's earnings were tiny, so it misleads as a red flag (Day 119). P/E: a normal P/E differs a lot by sector (a bank near 10, software near 40), and it doesn't predict a 2-week move. P/E is on the Value tab.

cardTexts.card-mr-read: 🔄 Mean-Reversion Read ⚙ FORWARD-TESTED A separate question: is this a short, sharp dip worth buying for a bounce? No signal Blocked by: it is below its 200-day average. Buying the dip needs all four to pass Has it dropped hard over the last 2 days? ✓ 2-day RSI 1.4 needs under 10 (a very sharp drop) sharp drop sharp rise RSI(2) scores recent momentum from 0 to 100, weighted mostly to the last 2 days. Low = it just fell fast. High = it just rose fast. Is it in an uptrend? ✗ 19.7% below its 200-day average needs to be above it below above The 200-day average is the usual line between an uptrend and a downtrend. Is the price high enough? ✓ $29.00 needs above $10 This skips penny stocks. Does it trade enough to get in and out? ✓ $28.1M traded on an average day needs above $25M Average of the last 20 days. Enough trading means you can get in and out. Checked on the 2026-11-19 close. How this read was formed What it is: Larry Connors' RSI(2) system ("Short Term Trading Strategies That Work"). RSI(2) scores recent momentum from 0 to 100, weighted mostly to the last 2 days; below 10 means a sharp, short drop. It buys that drop only while the stock is above its 200-day average, so it doesn't buy a falling knife. The four rules: the 2-day RSI below 10, close above the 200-day average, price above $10, and average daily trading above $25M (so you can get in and out cleanly). All four must pass. Track record: the rules were tested across many stocks with fills at the next open (what you can actually do). That record is about the system, not this stock. Independent of the Technical Read: a stock can pass most trend checks there and show No signal here, or the other way round. They answer different questions, and neither gates the other.
